Warning! This page contains spoilers from Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu. Caution is advised. [Hide] Difficult to see. Always in motion is the future. This page contains information about a confirmed future film. The content of the page may change dramatically as the product release approaches and more information becomes available. [Hide] "If you're searching for new adventures, 'this is the way'" ―Poster tagline[4] Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu, marketed simply as The Mandalorian and Grogu, is an upcoming live-action Star Wars film, scheduled for release in theaters on May 22, 2026. The film, directed by Jon Favreau, written by Favreau Dave Filoni and Noah Kloor, and produced by Favreau, Kathleen Kennedy, Filoni, and Ian Bryce, takes place between the events of Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi and Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens. It continues and is a spinoff of the Disney+ series The Mandalorian. In The Mandalorian and Grogu, the characters of Din Djarin (the titular "Mandalorian") and Grogu embark on a new adventure. The film stars Pedro Pascal, reprising his role as Din Djarin, and Sigourney Weaver. Ludwig Göransson, the original composer of The Mandalorian, returns to score the film. The film is the first in a new slate of Star Wars films and takes place in the same timeline as the ongoing Disney+ series The Mandalorian, a fourth season of which is still in development, and Star Wars: Ahsoka. 1 Publisher's summary 2 Development 3 Release and reception 4 Adaptations and tie-in media 5 Media 5.1 Content gallery 6 Credits 7 Appearances 8 Sources 9 Notes and references 10 External links Publisher's summary The Mandalorian, a lone bounty hunter, is tasked with capturing Grogu, a mysterious and adorable creature. Instead, he forms a strong bond with Grogu and strives to protect him from various threats, exploring his evolving purpose in a post-Empire galaxy.[6] Development "Dave Filoni and Jon Favreau have a new vision, continuing on with a Mandalorian movie." ―Giancarlo Esposito[7] The Mandalorian and Grogu was announced, originally as The Mandalorian & Grogu, on January 9, 2024 on StarWars.com with a conceptual sketch by veteran illustrator Ryan Church, along with an announcement of a second season of the television series Star Wars: Ahsoka.[1] A fourth season of The Mandalorian is also reportedly still in development.[8] However, series actor Giancarlo Esposito suggested the film was part of "a new vision" for The Mandalorian.[7] On May 7, 2019, Disney revealed their future movie release schedule, including a set of three untitled new Star Wars films, one of which had a scheduled release date of December 20, 2024.[9] The Star Wars Show also reported on the news on May 15.[10] On July 23, 2020, after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, the film was delayed to December 19, 2025.[11] After the start of the 2023 Writers Guild of America strike, Disney shifted their theatrical film release slate, with the film being pushed to its current release date of May 22, 2026.[12] A film directed by Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy occupied this release slot until The Mandalorian & Grogu was announced.[13] Star Wars Insider 224 revealed the initial film logo was the same as the one for The Mandalorian Season Three.[14] Principal photography was scheduled to begin in June 2024 in California,[15] and was expected to last for 92 days and have approximately 54 cast members, 3,500 background extras, and 500 crew members.[16] David Klein returned as director of photography from the The Mandalorian.[17] The Mandalorian and Grogu aimed to be the first Star Wars filmed to be filmed entierly in California.[16] During the D23 2024 on August 10 of that year, it was revealed that the film had entered production[12] several weeks prior[18] and a new logo was revealed[19] in addition to a teaser that was shown to the audience which showed the reappearance of Garazeb Orrelios from Star Wars Rebels and The Mandalorian season three and Anzellans.[12] Later that same month, Sigourney Weaver revealed that she had joined the cast of of the film, but hadn't yet started filming.[20] Additional footage was shown to audiences at D23 Brasil 2024 on November 9.[21] Filming had wrapped by by early December.[22] The final writing credits, consisting of Jon Favreau & Dave Filoni & Noah Kloor, were revealed by the Writer's Guild of America West on February 17, 2026.[3] Release and reception The Mandalorian and Grogu is scheduled for release on May 22, 2026.[12] The first teaser trailer was released on September 22, 2025.[4] A short advertisement, entitled "A New Journey Begins," aired during Super Bowl LX on February 8, 2026,[23] with another trailer was released on February 22.[24] Pascal and Weaver presented the awards for Best Production Design and Best Visual Effects at the 98th Academy Awards on March 15. Their presentation was accompanied by an appearance of Grogu seated next to actress Kate Hudson in the audience.[25] Adaptations and tie-in media During D23 2024 it was also announced that alongside the release of the movie, Millennium Falcon: Smuggler's Run will be updated to include a new mission featuring Djarin, Grogu, Tatooine, Endor and Cloud City, which takes place off camera from the film.[26] The reference book Star Wars: The Mandalorian Visual Guide, written by Pablo Hidalgo,[27] will release prior to the film on April 2, 2026 in the UK[28] and May 19 in the US.[29] Various other tie-ins and merchendise will also be released as part of the Star Wars: "Most Wanted" campaign.[30] Media Content gallery Credits Appearances By type [Show] Characters Organisms Droid models
